title: How Many Crows?
summary: A skeptical visiting nobleman challenges Birbal to verify his famous bird count. Birbal teaches him that truth requires evidence, not mere contradiction.
full_text:
Following Birbal's famous answer regarding the crows of Agra, an arrogant nobleman from Kashmir arrived at the imperial court. Jealous of Birbal's towering reputation, the nobleman sneered before Emperor Akbar: 'Your Majesty, it is easy to give a fanciful number when one knows nobody can verify it. Birbal merely invented fifty-two thousand crows out of thin air. A true counselor speaks only of what can be proven!'

Akbar looked at Birbal with twinkling eyes. 'Birbal, our esteemed guest disputes your calculation. How do you defend your honor?'

Birbal remained calm and unruffled. He bowed toward the visiting nobleman and said with polite warmth: 'My lord speaks with admirable caution. Truth is indeed sacred. Therefore, I propose a fair trial. The nobleman himself shall lead three hundred imperial scribes into the streets of Agra tomorrow at dawn to count every crow.'

'Gladly!' the nobleman proclaimed. 'I shall prove your claim false before dusk!'

'However,' Birbal added gently, 'as a man of strict proof, my lord must ensure two conditions. First, while counting, he must confirm that no mother crow lays an egg that hatches during the day, for a newly hatched chick would alter the count. Second, he must certify that no crow perishes from old age or flies across the city gate to peck at grain outside the walls during the census.'

The Kashmiri nobleman stood frozen. 'How can any mortal control when a wild bird hatches, flies, or dies?'

'Precisely,' Birbal answered softly. 'When a man demands absolute certainty regarding matters subject to perpetual change, he chases smoke with a sieve. Wisdom lies in recognizing the difference between meaningful knowledge and pointless wrangling.'

The Emperor nodded in agreement and the nobleman, thoroughly humbled, offered Birbal his sincere respect. Akbar commended his minister for showing that true intelligence disarms pompous doubt with effortless grace.
